drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Passing waves | Fix, pass, support
drills.players: 3 attackers, 2 passive defenders; rotate after each run.
drills.objective: Show two consecutive backward passes, realistic support depth, straightening and a support finish.
drills.safety: Non-contact demonstration. Defenders may make an agreed light touch only. No tackles in this practice.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · attack upfield — Three attackers are staggered behind the ball; defenders are passive.
2. First wave · draw D1 — A1 carries straight at D1; A2 holds support depth.
3. PASS · release backwards — A1 releases to A2 behind the ball, not forwards.
4. Second wave · fix D2 — A2 straightens towards D2; A3 stays deeper and wide.
5. PASS · attack the outside — A2 passes backwards to the supporting A3.
6. Finish · run straight — A3 accelerates into the channel; both passers support.
7. Reset · rotate roles — Freeze the finish; ask where both passes travelled. Return to setup between repetitions.
drills.coaching: Run straight to engage the defender, keep the receiver behind the ball, pass backwards and follow in support. Avoid drifting across the pitch.
drills.questions: Who fixes each defender? Are both receivers behind the passer? Why does the first passer continue supporting?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Contact | Tackle, release, present, play
drills.players: Carrier, defender, two supporting attackers, qualified coach.
drills.equipment: 1 ball; boundary cones; safe contact area.
drills.objective: Demonstrate controlled tackle sequence, prompt release, backward ball presentation and a legal support arrival.
drills.safety: Qualified coach-led controlled demonstration only, following current RFU U10 laws and tackle safety guidance. Animation is not a physical tackling tutorial. No high tackles, diving or dangerous clear-outs. Rehearse without contact first.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · controlled pairing — Carrier and defender face each other. Two teammates wait behind the carrier.
2. Track safely · shorten steps — Both approach at walking pace under coach supervision.
3. Contact demonstration · controlled ground — Coach demonstrates the approved low, controlled tackle. Never use this animation as technique instruction.
4. RELEASE · tackler clear — D1 releases promptly and gets clear. A1 stays grounded.
5. PRESENT · back to own team — A1 places the ball close to the body on the support side; no throw or forward transfer.
6. Support · on feet, from own side — A2 arrives from the attacking side, stays on feet and collects the available ball. No ruck has formed in this illustration.
7. Play away · continuity — A2 carries away, A3 tracks in support, the tackled player remains down until safe to recover.
8. Recover and reset — The coach resets all roles and checks everyone is ready before the next repetition.
drills.coaching: Tackler releases and moves clear. Grounded carrier makes the ball available to their own side. Support approaches on feet from their side. Do not pick up a ball once a ruck has formed.
drills.questions: Who releases? Which way should the tackled player present? When must supporters stay on their feet?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Contact pads | Approach, hit, recover
drills.players: Two attackers and a qualified coach holding a shield; others wait outside lane.
drills.objective: Show a safe supervised progression from tracking to controlled contact against a shield and recovery into support.
drills.safety: Coach-led pad practice only; use a properly held shield and current club/RFU contact coaching standards. Do not coach head placement or tackle mechanics from an overhead animation. Avoid uncontrolled impact and collisions.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · pad holder ready — Coach holds the shield; only one attacker enters the lane.
2. Approach · walk then jog — A1 moves at coach-approved pace and checks the holder is set.
3. Controlled pad contact — Demonstrate position and control against the shield, not a full-speed collision.
4. Hold balance · release pressure — A1 regains balance; coach holds the shield stationary.
5. Exit to the side — A1 clears the lane; A2 waits for the coach signal.
6. Second player · approach on signal — A2 starts only when the pad holder is reset and lane is empty.
7. Reset and rotate — Pause before second contact, return to start, repeat under supervision.
drills.coaching: Controlled approach, balanced footwork, eyes up, coach-directed shield contact, recover balance and reset. One participant at a time.
drills.questions: Is the holder ready? Is the lane clear? Can the player stop and recover under control?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U8 Tag | TAG, pass, return, play
drills.players: Three attacking tag-belt wearers and two tag defenders.
drills.equipment: Tag belts with two strips per player, rugby ball, cones.
drills.objective: Explain the tag, immediate pass and returning the strip before either player rejoins.
drills.safety: U7/U8 RFU tag-rule teaching example, not tackle rugby. No contact, pushing or blocking; the tagged player must pass within the applicable rule and replace the tag before rejoining.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · tag belts checked — A1 carries; all players wear correctly fitted tag belts.
2. Run and track — A1 advances; D1 tracks safely for a tag, not a tackle.
3. TAG! · stop and call — D1 removes one strip from A1 and shouts TAG; A1 stops.
4. PASS · tagged carrier releases — A1 passes backwards to A2; D1 holds the removed strip up.
5. RETURN · restore the strip — D1 returns the strip to A1; both restore belts before rejoining.
6. Keep playing · second channel — A2 attacks the next space. A1 only rejoins after replacing the strip.
7. Pass to support and finish — A2 passes backwards to A3 who continues into the wide channel.
drills.coaching: Tagger calls TAG and holds the strip aloft. The tagged player stops and passes, and the tagger returns the removed strip. Both respect the return-to-play requirement.
drills.questions: What must the tagger shout? Who returns the strip? Can either player rejoin without the tag properly restored?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · Touch rugby | Touch, rollball, retreat
drills.players: Three attackers and two defenders, with an instructor/referee.
drills.equipment: Ball, cones, clearly indicated touch mark.
drills.objective: Illustrate an England Touch-style rollball and defensive retreat, then a second attacking phase.
drills.safety: Non-contact Touch training, NOT RFU U10 contact laws or RFU U7/U8 tag laws. Use the exact touch competition's rules; no tackling or forceful touches.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · Touch code — Explain: this is formal Touch practice, not RFU U10 match restart law.
2. Attack · draw a touch — A1 runs into D1's channel; A2 remains behind as the prospective half.
3. TOUCH · freeze the mark — Light touch by D1; ball carrier stops. Do not pass after a completed touch.
4. Retreat · defenders get onside — Defenders move back the required 7 m before involving themselves. A1 prepares the rollball.
5. ROLLBALL · at the mark — A1 plays the ball back through the legs at the mark; A2 becomes the half.
6. Half passes · next phase — A2, acting as half, passes backwards to A3. Avoid claiming an automatic right for the half to score.
7. Continue · attack space — A3 accelerates into open space while defenders advance from their onside positions.
drills.coaching: On a valid touch, the touched attacker returns to the mark and executes a rollball. Defenders retreat at least 7 m under England Touch introductory rules and wait until the half touches the ball before moving forward. The half cannot score and loses possession if touched.
drills.questions: Where is the touch mark? Are the defenders back 7 m? Is the half allowed to score? Which competition rule set are we playing?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Offside | Free pass and 7 m retreat
drills.players: 3 attackers, 3 defenders, one coach as referee.
drills.objective: Teach that defenders must stay back the U10 free-pass retreat distance and wait for the pass before advancing.
drills.safety: Walking-speed, non-contact rehearsal. Use current RFU U10 rules and an accurately measured 7 m retreat. The animated diagram is schematic; verify actual distances on the pitch.
drills.instructions:
1. Free pass · set the mark — Attacking team at mark. Defenders begin behind their retreat line; coach checks real spacing.
2. HOLD · defenders wait — Before release the defensive line is static and onside. Ask when they may move.
3. FREE PASS · ball travels backwards — A1 passes to supporting A2; defensive advance starts after the ball leaves the hands.
4. Advance together · stay connected — D1, D2, D3 advance in a connected line without running early.
5. Decision · carrier fixes middle — A2 carries straight; defenders keep connection and communicate.
6. Backward pass · release outside — A2 draws D2 and gives A3 a backward pass into the outside channel.
7. Freeze · review the rule — Pause on the connected line; compare actual free-pass retreat distances on the pitch.
drills.coaching: Identify the mark, measure 7 m, wait behind the retreat line and advance only when the ball is passed. Do not confuse this with Touch rollball retreat or ruck offside.
drills.questions: Where is the mark? How far must defenders retreat? Can they rush before the free pass? Which passing direction is permitted?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Decisions | Carry or give the overlap?
drills.players: Three attackers versus two passive touch defenders.
drills.objective: Compare two sound decisions at the same freeze-frame: carry if space remains, or pass backwards if the defender commits.
drills.safety: Non-contact 3v2 coaching demonstration; touch only, no tackle. The options are coached choices, not automatic AI decisions.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · 3 v 2 — A1 carries and A2/A3 hold width and depth.
2. Commit D1 · straighten — A1 fixes D1 while supporting runners track inside.
3. Pass behind · A2 receives — A1 passes backwards; A2 attacks the space between defenders.
4. DECISION · what does D2 do? — Freeze. Two alternatives start from this identical moment.
5. A · D2 holds wide: carry — D2 marks A3, leaving A2 an inside channel. A2 carries straight.
6. A · finish with support — A2 breaks through, A1 stays available behind.
drills.coaching: Look at defender hips, straighten first, keep support behind; release only if the defender has committed.
drills.questions: What is D2 doing? When is carrying best? Where must the support runner stand?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.

drills.title: SHOWCASE · U10 Continuity | Three phases, one team
drills.players: Four attackers and two passive touch defenders.
drills.objective: Show three successive phases of attack with backward passing, depth, support and a clean finish.
drills.safety: Non-contact progression with light-touch defence only; no breakdown, tackle, or physical clear-out is implied.
drills.instructions:
1. Setup · start the first phase — A1 carries with A2, A3, A4 in supporting lanes.
2. Phase 1 · A1 commits — A1 engages D1 and A2 holds back for a legal pass.
3. Release to A2 — A1 passes backward to A2, then reloads into support.
4. Phase 2 · A2 straightens — A2 engages D2; A3 remains deeper.
5. Release to A3 — Second backward pass enters the wider channel.
6. Phase 3 · A3 runs at shoulder — A3 straightens; A4 stays in depth, never ahead of the passer.
7. Outside pass to A4 — A3 releases a third backward pass; A4 takes the ball behind A3.
8. Final break · support behind — A4 reaches space with A3 tracking in support.
drills.coaching: Keep the ball alive, straighten before passing, stay behind the carrier and reload on each new phase.
drills.questions: How do we recycle support without crowding? What changes when defence drifts?
drills.notes: Showcase teaching animation: coaches must check current competition/age-grade law and run a safety assessment. Stage text describes the actual saved movement; use normal-speed and follow-action camera for promos.
